<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><br /></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">76</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">DOMTAR CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">DECEMBER 31, 2019</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">(IN MILLIONS OF DOLLARS, UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED</span>)</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 7. PENSION PLANS AND OTHER POST-RETIREMENT BENEFIT PLANS (CONTINUED)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000369_dcnt_021b7cba-6394-4985-839b-206ebb8648e4" continuedAt="F_000369_dcnt_be3ab905-2aa8-4826-b10e-ecce894ca7e2">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company used a full yield curve approach to estimate the current service and interest cost components of net periodic benefit cost for Canadian pension plans and U.S. funded pension plans. The estimate of these components is made by applying the specific spot rates along the yield curve used in the determination of the benefit obligation to the relevant projected cash flows.&#160; </span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For the U.S. unfunded pension plan and other post-retirement benefits, given materiality, the current service and interest cost components were estimated using a single weighted-average discount rate derived from the yield curve for each unfunded pension plan or based on each post-retirement plans&#8217; projected cash flows. The discount rate of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000946" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationDiscountRate" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapRetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis_countryUS_20191231" decimals="3" scale="-2">4.2</ix:nonFraction>% for U.S. unfunded plans is obtained by incorporating the plans&#8217; expected cash flows in the Mercer Yield Curve.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For Canadian plans, short-term yields to maturity are derived from actual AA rated corporate bond yield data. For longer terms, extrapolated data is used. The extrapolated data are created by adding a term-based spread over long provincial bond yields. For U.S. funded plans, the rates are taken from the Mercer Yield Curve which is based on bonds rated AA by Moody&#8217;s or Standard &#38; Poor&#8217;s, excluding callable bonds, bonds of less than a minimum issue size, and certain other bonds. The universe of bonds also includes private placement (traded in reliance on Rule 144A and which are at least <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000947" name="ufs:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUniversalBondsMaturity" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapRetirementPlanSponsorLocationAxis_countryUS_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">two years</ix:nonNumeric> from issuance), make whole, and foreign corporation (denominated in U.S. dollars) bonds.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Effective January 1, 2020, the Company will use <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000948" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapSubsequentEventTypeAxis_us-gaapSubsequentEventMember_20200101_20200101" decimals="3" scale="-2">4.8</ix:nonFraction>% (2019 &#8211; <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000949" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="3" scale="-2">5.2</ix:nonFraction>%&#59; 2018 &#8211; <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000950" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingNetPeriodicBenefitCostExpectedLongTermReturnOnAssets" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="3" scale="-2">5.2</ix:nonFraction>%) as the expected return on plan assets, which reflects the current view of long-term investment returns. The overall expected long-term rate of return on plan assets is based on management's best estimate of the long-term returns of the major asset classes (cash and cash equivalents, equities, and bonds) weighted by the actual allocation of assets at the measurement date, net of expenses. This rate includes an equity risk premium over government bond returns for equity investments and a value-added premium for the contribution to returns from active management. The sources used to determine management's best estimate of long-term returns are numerous and include country specific bond yields, which may be derived from the market using local bond indices or by analysis of the local bond market, and country-specific inflation and investment market expectations derived from market data and analysts' or governments' expectations, as applicable.</p><ix:continuation id="F_000432_cnt_1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 7. PENSION PLANS AND OTHER POST-RETIREMENT BENEFIT PLANS (CONTINUED)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000369_dcnt_be3ab905-2aa8-4826-b10e-ecce894ca7e2" continuedAt="F_000369_dcnt_a13ecfc1-d77d-4994-aeed-765d2d732a8a">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENT</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures Topic of FASB ASC 820 establishes a fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value into three levels. A financial instrument&#8217;s categorization within the fair value hierarchy is based upon the lowest level of input that is available and significant to the fair value measurement.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2019, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001158" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">20</ix:nonFraction> million of tax credits, mainly research and experimentation credits, which impacted the effective tax rate. Arkansas legislation changes were passed in 2019 which reduced the state tax rate and changed how the apportionment factor is calculated. This resulted in a deferred state tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001159" name="us-gaap:DeferredStateAndLocalIncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">4</ix:nonFraction> million for the Company. Additionally, a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001160" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationChangeInDeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">5</ix:nonFraction> million was recorded on state attributes the Company does not expect to utilize before they expire.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of the deemed mandatory repatriation tax requirement of the U.S. Tax Reform, the Company has taxed its undistributed foreign earnings as of December 31, 2017, at reduced tax rates. After completing its evaluation of the U.S. Tax Reform&#8217;s impact on its business operations, the Company has determined that it is no longer indefinitely reinvested in these undistributed foreign earnings as well as foreign earnings after December 31, 2017. As such, as of December 31, 2019, the Company has recorded a deferred tax liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001161" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_ufsForeignCountryAndStateJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">12</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001162" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_ufsForeignCountryAndStateJurisdictionMember_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">10</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2018) for foreign withholding tax and various state income taxes associated with future repatriation of these earnings. This additional $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001163" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationDeferredTaxesOnForeignEarnings" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">2</ix:nonFraction> million tax expense impacted the effective tax rate for 2019 ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001164" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationDeferredTaxesOnForeignEarnings" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">10</ix:nonFraction> million for 2018).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2018, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001165" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">19</ix:nonFraction> million of tax credits, mainly research and experimentation credits, which impacted the effective tax rate. The effective tax rate was also impacted by the cancellation of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001166" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationNetOperatingLossCancellation" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">9</ix:nonFraction> million, after-tax, of net operating losses in a foreign jurisdiction. This was offset by the reversal of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001167" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationChangeInDeferredTaxAssetsReversalOfValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">9</ix:nonFraction> million of valuation allowance on these same net operating losses. Additionally, a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001168" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapValuationAllowanceByDeferredTaxAssetAxis_ufsOperatingLossesMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">1</ix:nonFraction> million was recorded on new operating losses in 2018 for a net benefit pertaining to valuation allowance movements of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001169" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationChangeInDeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6">8</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><br /></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">84</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">DOMTAR CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">DECEMBER 31, 2019</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">(IN MILLIONS OF DOLLARS, UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED</span>)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 10. INCOME TAXES (CONTINUED)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000372_dcnt_fc6ee786-d468-4844-9e6a-ba41aef40303" continuedAt="F_000372_dcnt_bbe326cf-da82-4079-bb58-0ab0127e661a">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 22, 2017, the U.S. Tax Reform was signed into law. The U.S. Tax Reform significantly changed U.S. tax law for businesses by, among other things, lowering the maximum federal corporate income tax rate from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001170" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001171" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction>% effective January 1, 2018, implementing a territorial tax system, and imposing a one-time deemed repatriation tax on accumulated foreign earnings. As a result of the U.S. Tax Reform, the Company recorded a net tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001172" name="ufs:NetIncomeTaxBenefitExpenseFromUSTaxCutsAndJobsAct" contextRef="C_0001381531_20171221_20171222" decimals="-6" scale="6">140</ix:nonFraction> million in 2017 when the legislation was enacted. This consisted of a provisional tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001173" name="ufs:IncomeTaxBenefitFromUSTaxCutsAndJobsAct" contextRef="C_0001381531_20171221_20171222" decimals="-6" scale="6">186</ix:nonFraction> million relating to the revaluation of the Company&#8217;s ending net deferred tax liabilities and a provisional expense of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001174" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationAdjustmentToDeemedMandatoryRepatriationTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001381531_20171221_20171222" decimals="-6" scale="6">46</ix:nonFraction> million related to the deemed repatriation tax, which the Company elected to pay over <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001180" name="ufs:NumberOfYearsElectToPayTax" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">eight years</ix:nonNumeric>. Additionally, Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 118 (&#8220;SAB 118&#8221;) was issued to address the application in situations when a registrant does not have the necessary information available, prepared, or analyzed in reasonable detail to complete the accounting for certain income tax effects of the U.S. Tax Reform. December 22, 2018 marked the end of the measurement period for purposes of SAB 118. As such, the Company completed its analysis, including currently available legislative updates, and recorded an additional tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001175" name="ufs:NetIncomeTaxBenefitExpenseFromUSTaxCutsAndJobsAct" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">13</ix:nonFraction> million for the year ended December 31, 2018. Of this benefit, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001176" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationAdjustmentToDeemedMandatoryRepatriationTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6">7</ix:nonFraction> million related to adjustments to the deemed mandatory repatriation tax and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001177" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationRevaluationOfNetDeferredTaxLiabilities" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">6</ix:nonFraction> million related to the revaluation of the Company&#8217;s net deferred tax liabilities. The $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001178" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationRevaluationOfNetDeferredTaxLiabilities" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">6</ix:nonFraction> million benefit for the revaluation of the net deferred tax liabilities is included in the &#8220;Tax rate changes&#8221; above, along with $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001179" name="ufs:NetIncomeTaxBenefitAdditionalFromUSTaxCutsAndJobsAct" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">3</ix:nonFraction> million of additional tax benefits relating to 2018 law changes in Sweden and various U.S. states.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2017, the Company recorded a goodwill impairment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001181" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">578</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million with minimal tax benefit which impacted the effective tax rate by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001182" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationNondeductibleExpenseImpairmentLosses" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">200</ix:nonFraction> million. The effective tax rate for 2017 was also significantly impacted by the Company&#8217;s foreign operations being taxed at lower statutory tax rates and by the Company recording $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001183" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationTaxCreditsResearch" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">24</ix:nonFraction> million of current tax credits, mainly research and experimentation credits.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of the corporate tax rate reduction, from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001184" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001185" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction>%, due to the U.S. Tax Reform, the Company revalued its ending net deferred tax liabilities, and recognized a provisional tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001186" name="ufs:IncomeTaxBenefitFromUSTaxCutsAndJobsAct" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">186</ix:nonFraction> million in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statement of Earnings (Loss) and Comprehensive Income (Loss) for the year ended December 31, 2017. This, combined with a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001187" name="ufs:IncomeTaxBenefitFromOtherChangesInUSLaw" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">2</ix:nonFraction> million tax benefit from other changes in law in certain U.S. states earlier in the year, impacted the effective tax rate for 2017.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 22, 2017, the SEC staff issued SAB 118 to address the application in situations when a registrant does not have the necessary information available, prepared, or analyzed in reasonable detail to complete the accounting for certain income tax effects of the U.S. Tax Reform. SAB 118 provides guidance which allows companies to use a measurement period, similar to that used in business combinations, to account for the impacts of the U.S. Tax Reform. The U.S. Tax Reform provides for a mandatory one-time deemed repatriation tax on the Company&#8217;s undistributed foreign earnings and profits. The Company recorded a provisional repatriation tax amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001188" name="ufs:IncomeTaxReconciliationAdjustmentToDeemedMandatoryRepatriationTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">46</ix:nonFraction> million, which impacted the 2017 tax rate. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are based on tax rates that are expected to be in effect in future periods when deferred items are expected to reverse. Changes in tax rates or tax laws affect the expected future benefit or expense. The effect of such changes that occurred during each of the last three fiscal years is included in &#8220;Tax rate changes&#8221; disclosed under the effective income tax rate reconciliation shown above.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">85</p>

The Company has other foreign net operating losses and deduction limitations of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001222" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_ufsDeductionLimitationsMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">195</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million which may be carried forward indefinitely.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In assessing the realizability of deferred tax assets, management considers whether it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income during periods in which temporary differences become deductible.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company evaluates the realization of deferred tax assets on a quarterly basis. Evaluating the need for an amount of a valuation allowance for deferred tax assets often requires significant judgment. All available evidence, both positive and negative, is considered when determining whether, based on the weight of that evidence, a valuation allowance is needed. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management believes that it is more likely than not that the results of future operations will generate sufficient taxable income to realize the deferred tax assets, with the exception of certain state credits for which a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001223" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapValuationAllowanceByDeferredTaxAssetAxis_ufsStateTaxCreditsMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">11</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million exists at December 31, 2019, and certain foreign loss carryforwards for which a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001224" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsOperatingLossCarryforwardsForeign" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">10</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million exists at December 31, 2019. Of this amount, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001225" name="ufs:ImpactOnIncomeTaxExpenseRelatedToChangesToValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million unfavorably impacted tax expense and the effective tax rate for 2019 (2018 &#8211; $(<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001226" name="ufs:ImpactOnIncomeTaxExpenseRelatedToChangesToValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6">8</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;million&#59; 2017 &#8211; $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001227" name="ufs:ImpactOnIncomeTaxExpenseRelatedToChangesToValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million).</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><br /></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">86</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">DOMTAR CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">DECEMBER 31, 2019</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">(IN MILLIONS OF DOLLARS, UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED</span>)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 10. INCOME TAXES (CONTINUED)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000372_dcnt_4b8688d2-b509-4888-aa6b-6e52a15d2251">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2019, the Company has recorded a deferred tax liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001228" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_ufsForeignCountryAndStateJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">12</ix:nonFraction> million for foreign withholding tax and various state income taxes associated with the repatriation of earnings subject to the repatriation tax as well as future repatriation of its unremitted foreign earnings. The Company has not provided for deferred taxes on the outside basis differences in its investments in its foreign subsidiaries that are unrelated to unremitted earnings as it estimates that the deferred tax liability, in combination with the repatriation tax amount, covers all tax liabilities with foreign investments to date. The Company remains indefinitely reinvested in the outside basis differences of its foreign subsidiaries.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The U.S. Tax Reform also includes a base erosion provision for GILTI. Beginning in 2018, the GILTI provisions require the Company to include in its U.S. income tax return, earnings of foreign subsidiaries that are in excess of an allowable return on the tangible assets of the foreign subsidiaries. The Company is required to make an accounting policy election to either (1) treat taxes due related to GILTI as a current period expense when incurred or (2) factor such amounts into the measurement of deferred taxes. The Company has elected to account for any taxes associated with GILTI as a period cost.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ACCOUNTING FOR UNCERTAINTY IN INCOME TAXES</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000443" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsRollForwardTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December&#160;31, 2019, the Company had gross unrecognized tax benefits of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001229" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">29</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001230" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001381531_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">32</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001231" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001381531_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">37</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for 2018 and 2017, respectively). If recognized in 2020, these tax benefits would impact the effective tax rate. These amounts represent the gross amount of exposure in individual jurisdictions and do not reflect any additional benefits expected to be realized if such positions were sustained, such as federal deduction that could be realized if an unrecognized state deduction was not sustained. These amounts are included in Deferred income taxes and other on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>

The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties, if any, related to unrecognized tax benefits as a component of tax expense.&#160;The Company believes it is reasonably possible that up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001255" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefits" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtStatementScenarioAxis_srtScenarioForecastMember_20201231" decimals="-6" scale="6">6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of its unrecognized tax benefits may be recognized by December 31, 2020, which could significantly impact the effective tax rate. However, the amount and timing of the recognition of these benefits is subject to some uncertainty.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The major jurisdictions where the Company and its subsidiaries will file tax returns for 2019, in addition to filing one consolidated U.S. federal income tax return, are Canada, Sweden and Spain. The Company and its subsidiaries will also file returns in various other countries in Europe and Asia as well as various U.S. states and Canadian provinces. At December&#160;31, 2019, the Company&#8217;s subsidiaries are subject to foreign federal income tax examinations for the tax years 2008 through 2018, with federal years prior to 2016 being closed from a cash tax liability standpoint in the U.S., but the loss carryforwards can be adjusted in any open year where the loss has been utilized. The Company does not anticipate that adjustments stemming from these audits would result in a significant change to the results of its operations and financial condition.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">DOMTAR CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">DECEMBER 31, 2019</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">(IN MILLIONS OF DOLLARS, UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED</span>)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000375" name="ufs:LesseeDisclosureOfLeasesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000375_dcnt_d520bf95-2c7b-4aff-a488-be615f1784fe">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="Note_Leases">NOTE 13.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:center;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:40%;margin-right:40%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">LEASES</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the normal course of business, the Company enters into operating and finance leases mainly for manufacturing and warehousing facilities, corporate offices, motor vehicles, mobile equipment and manufacturing equipment. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">While the Company&#8217;s lease payments are generally fixed over the lease term, some leases may include price escalation terms that are fixed at the lease commencement date.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has remaining lease terms ranging from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001285" name="ufs:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1</ix:nonNumeric> year to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001286" name="ufs:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceRemainingLeaseTerm" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">14</ix:nonNumeric> years, some of which may include options to extend the leases for up to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001287" name="ufs:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceLeasesExtendableTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years, and some of which may include options to terminate the leases within <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001288" name="ufs:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceLeasesTerminableTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">1</ix:nonNumeric> year. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December 31, 2019<span style="color:#000000;">, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001289" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLeasehold" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">9</ix:nonFraction> million of impairment of operating lease right-of-use assets under Impairment of long-lived assets on the Consolidated Statement of Earnings (Loss) and Comprehensive Income (Loss).</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">DOMTAR CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;font-size:12pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">DECEMBER 31, 2019</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">(IN MILLIONS OF DOLLARS, UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED</span>)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000378" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000378_dcnt_469a40af-21b1-4af0-b176-82ef0ab8e91f">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="NOTE_16">NOTE 16.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:center;border-bottom:Solid 0.75pt;padding-bottom:1pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:40%;margin-right:40%;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CLOSURE AND RESTRUCTURING COSTS AND LIABILITY</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December&#160;31, 2019, the Company&#8217;s total provision for the withdrawal liabilities of its U.S. multiemployer plans was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001405" name="ufs:MultiemployerPlansWithdrawalObligationCurrentAccrual" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapMultiemployerPlanTypeAxis_ufsMultiEmployerPensionPlansMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">44</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Ashdown, Arkansas mill and Port Huron, Michigan mill</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 27, 2019, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved the decision to permanently shut down <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_ufsMachine" id="F_001406" name="ufs:NumberOfClosedPaperMachines" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190927_20190927" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> paper machines, which was announced on October 3, 2019. The closures took place at the Ashdown, Arkansas pulp and paper mill and the Port Huron, Michigan paper mill. These measures will reduce the Company&#8217;s annual uncoated freesheet paper capacity by approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrT" id="F_001407" name="ufs:ReductionInAnnualProductionCapacityOfPaper" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190927_20190927" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">204,000</ix:nonFraction> short tons, and resulted in a workforce reduction of approximately <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_ufsEmployee" id="F_001408" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedNumberOfPositionsEliminated" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190927_20190927" decimals="INF">100</ix:nonFraction> employees.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The closure of the Ashdown paper machine took effect immediately. The Ashdown mill will continue to operate <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_ufsMachine" id="F_001409" name="ufs:NumberOfOperatingPaperMachine" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillMember_20191003_20191003" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> paper machine with an annual uncoated freesheet paper production capacity of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrT" id="F_001410" name="ufs:AnnualProductionCapacityOfOperatingPaperMachine" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillMember_20191003_20191003" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">200,000</ix:nonFraction> short tons. Additionally, the mill operates a fluff pulp machine with the flexibility to produce softwood pulp depending on market conditions. As a result of the closure of the paper machine, the mill will produce an incremental <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrt" id="F_001411" name="ufs:IncrementalProductionOfSoftwoodAndFluffPulp" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillMember_20191003_20191003" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">70,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;ADMT of softwood and fluff pulp, which will ramp up over the course of 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The closure of the Port Huron paper machine took effect mid-November. The Port Huron mill will continue to produce a variety of technical and specialty papers for a broad range of customers utilizing <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_ufsMachine" id="F_001412" name="ufs:NumberOfOperatingPaperMachine" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190927_20190927" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">three</ix:nonFraction> machines with a total annual production capacity of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_utrT" id="F_001413" name="ufs:AnnualProductionCapacityOfOperatingPaperMachine" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190927_20190927" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">95,000</ix:nonFraction> short tons.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For the year ended December 31, 2019, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001414" name="us-gaap:RestructuringReserveAcceleratedDepreciation" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_ufsImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsMember_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">32</ix:nonFraction> million of accelerated depreciation under Impairment of long-lived assets and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001415" name="us-gaap:RestructuringReserveAcceleratedDepreciation" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_ufsDepreciationAndAmortizationMember_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">1</ix:nonFraction> million of accelerated depreciation under Depreciation and amortization, on the Consolidated Statement of Earnings (Loss) and Comprehensive Income (Loss). Additionally, the Company recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001416" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">3</ix:nonFraction> million of severance and termination costs, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001417" name="us-gaap:InventoryWriteDown" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of inventory obsolescence, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001418" name="us-gaap:OtherRestructuringCosts" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillAndPortHuronMichiganMillMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">2</ix:nonFraction> million of other costs, under Closure and restructuring costs. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Concurrently, with the Ashdown paper machine closure and related workforce reduction, management negotiated a voluntary early retirement program to reduce costs and put the mill in a stronger cost position in the long-term. The Company additionally recorded $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001419" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapInvestmentTypeAxis_ufsAshdownArkansasMillMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">13</ix:nonFraction> million of severance and termination costs under Closure and restructuring costs.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Waco, Texas facility</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On November 1, 2018, the Company announced a margin improvement plan within the Personal Care Division. As part of this plan, the Board of Directors approved the permanent closure of its Waco, Texas Personal Care manufacturing and distribution facility, the relocation of certain of its manufacturing assets and a workforce reduction across the division. The Waco, Texas facility ceased operations during the second quarter of 2019.</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">DOMTAR CORPORATION</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">DECEMBER 31, 2019</span></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">(IN MILLIONS OF DOLLARS, UNLESS OTHERWISE NOTED</span>)</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman Bold;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 19. LONG-TERM DEBT (CONTINUED)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000381_dcnt_0717d7c0-e966-42e1-875d-8ac5bb924184">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">REVOLVING CREDIT FACILITY</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2018, the Company amended and restated its $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001654" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsCreditAgreementMember_20160818" decimals="INF" scale="6">700</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million unsecured revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Credit Agreement&#8221;) with certain domestic and foreign banks. The amendment extended the Credit Agreement&#8217;s maturity date from <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001653" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityExpirationDate1" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsAmendedCreditAgreementMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">August 18, 2021</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001652" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentMaturityDate" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsCreditAgreementMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">August 22, 2023</ix:nonNumeric>. The maturity date of the facility may be extended by <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001655" name="ufs:CreditFacilityExtendableTerm" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsCreditAgreementMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> and the lender commitments may be increased by up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001656" name="ufs:AmountOfLenderCommitmentsOnCreditFacility" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsCreditAgreementMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">400</ix:nonFraction> million, subject to lender approval and customary requirements.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings by the Company under the Credit Agreement are guaranteed by its significant domestic subsidiaries. Borrowings by certain foreign subsidiaries under the Credit Agreement are guaranteed by the Company, the Company&#8217;s significant domestic subsidiaries and certain of the Company&#8217;s significant foreign subsidiaries. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest at LIBOR, EURIBOR, Canadian bankers' acceptance or prime rate, as applicable, plus a margin linked to the Company&#8217;s credit rating.&#160;In addition, the Company pays facility fees quarterly at rates dependent on the Company's credit ratings.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001663" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCovenantDescription" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsCreditAgreementMember_20190101_20191231"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Credit Agreement contains customary covenants and events of default for transactions of this type, including two financial covenants: (i) an interest coverage ratio, as defined in the Credit Agreement, that must be maintained at a level of not less than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001657" name="ufs:DebtInstrumentInterestCoverageRatio" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_ufsCreditAgreementMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF">3</ix:nonFraction> to 1 and (ii) a leverage ratio, as defined in the Credit Agreement, that must be maintained at a level of not greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" qualifying material acquisitions). At December&#160;31, 2019, the Company was in compliance with these financial covenants, and had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001660" name="us-gaap:LineOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">80</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of borrowings outstanding under this facility (December&#160;31, 2018 &#8211; nil), leaving $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001662" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">620</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million available under this facility. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">TERM LOAN</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the third quarter of 2015, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Domtar borrowed $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001664" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_ufsTermLoanMember_20150930" decimals="-6" scale="6">300</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million under an unsecured <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001665" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentTerm" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_ufsTermLoanMember_20150701_20150930" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> year Term Loan Agreement with certain domestic banks. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the fourth quarter of 2018, the Term Loan was fully repaid.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RECEIVABLES SECURITIZATION</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001666" name="us-gaap:LineOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapSecuredDebtMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">150</ix:nonFraction> million receivables securitization facility. This facility was amended in November 2018 to extend the maturity date from March 2019 to November 2021. This facility provides additional liquidity to the Company to fund its operations or issue letters of credit. The costs under the program vary based on changes in interest rates and amounts utilized. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sales of receivables under this program are accounted for as secured borrowings. The program consists of the ongoing sale of most of the receivables of its domestic subsidiaries to a bankruptcy remote consolidated subsidiary which, in turn, transfers a senior beneficial interest in them to a special purpose entity managed by a financial institution for multiple sellers of receivables to support borrowings or the issue of letters of credit by the Company.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The program contains certain termination events, which include, but are not limited to, matters related to receivable performance, certain defaults occurring under the Credit Agreement, or the failure by Domtar to satisfy material obligations.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December&#160;31, 2019, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001667" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityCurrentBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">55</ix:nonFraction> million was borrowed and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001669" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">53</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of letters of credit were outstanding under this facility (2018 &#8211; $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001668" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityCurrentBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001381531_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001670" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" contextRef="C_0001381531_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">52</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively). At December&#160;31, 2019, the Company had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001671" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentUnusedBorrowingCapacityAmount" contextRef="C_0001381531_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapLetterOfCreditMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">25</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million unused and available under this facility.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2019, a net charge of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001672" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnSecuritizationOfFinancialAssets" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (2018 &#8211; $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001673" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnSecuritizationOfFinancialAssets" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#59; 2017 &#8211; $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001674" name="us-gaap:GainLossOnSecuritizationOfFinancialAssets" contextRef="C_0001381531_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million) resulted from the program described above and was included in Interest expense, net in the Consolidated Statements of Earnings (Loss) and Comprehensive Income (Loss).</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The asset retirement obligations are principally linked to landfill capping obligations and demolition of certain abandoned buildings. At December&#160;31, 2019, Domtar estimated the net present value of its asset retirement obligations to be $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001693" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligation" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">13</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (2018&#160;&#8211;&#160;$<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001694" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligation" contextRef="C_0001381531_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">12</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million)&#59; the present value is based on probability weighted undiscounted cash outflows of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001695" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationCashPaidToSettle" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">58</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million (2018&#160;&#8211;&#160;$<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001696" name="us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationCashPaidToSettle" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">59</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million). The majority of the asset retirement obligations are estimated to be settled prior to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001697" name="ufs:AssetRetirementObligationExpectedSettlementDate" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">December 31, 2059</ix:nonNumeric>. Domtar&#8217;s credit adjusted risk-free rates were used to calculate the net present value of the asset retirement obligations. The rates used vary between <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001698" name="ufs:CreditAdjustedRiskFreeRatesUsedToEvaluatePresentValueOfAssetRetirementObligations" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">4.7</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001699" name="ufs:CreditAdjustedRiskFreeRatesUsedToEvaluatePresentValueOfAssetRetirementObligations" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">12.0</ix:nonFraction>%, based on the prevailing rate at the moment of recognition of the liability and on its settlement period.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000461" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfAssetRetirementObligationsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">STOCK REPURCHASE PROGRAM</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors has authorized a stock repurchase program (&#8220;the Program&#8221;) of up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001744" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191104" decimals="INF" scale="9">1.3</ix:nonFraction> billion. On November 5, 2019, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved an increase to the Program from $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001745" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191104" decimals="INF" scale="9">1.3</ix:nonFraction> billion to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001746" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" contextRef="C_0001381531_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191105" decimals="INF" scale="9">1.6</ix:nonFraction> billion. At December&#160;31, 2019, the Company had approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001747" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchaseProgramRemainingAuthorizedRepurchaseAmount1" contextRef="C_0001381531_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">403</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of remaining availability under the Program. Under the Program, the Company is authorized to repurchase, from time to time, shares of its outstanding common stock on the open market or in privately negotiated transactions. The timing and amount of stock repurchases will depend on a variety of factors, including the market conditions as well as corporate and regulatory considerations. The Program may be suspended, modified or discontinued at any time, and the Company has no obligation to repurchase any amount of its common stock under the Program. The Program has no set expiration date. The Company repurchases its common stock in part to reduce the dilutive effects of stock options and awards, and to improve shareholders&#8217; returns.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company makes open market purchases of its common stock using general corporate funds. Additionally, the Company may enter into structured stock repurchase agreements with large financial institutions using general corporate funds in order to lower the average cost to acquire shares. The agreements would require the Company to make up-front payments to the counterparty financial institutions, which would result in either the receipt of stock at the beginning of the term of the agreements followed by a share adjustment at the maturity of the agreements, or the receipt of either stock or cash at the maturity of the agreements, depending upon the price of the stock.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2019, the Company repurchased <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001748" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">6,220,658</ix:nonFraction> shares at an average price of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001750" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockAcquiredAverageCostPerShare" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="2">35.29</ix:nonFraction> for a total cost of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001751" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockValueAcquiredCostMethod" contextRef="C_0001381531_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">219</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2018, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001749" name="us-gaap:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired" contextRef="C_0001381531_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction> shares repurchased under the Program.</p>
